correctness.rationale: Zeckendorf uniqueness identifies the slice with nonadjacent subsets of indices 2 through M (the maximum sum from those indices is F_(M+1)-1 by the largest-index recursion). On a complete Pisano block multiple all ordered coordinates have exactly the cycle law. Per coordinate pair the equal-index event has count L^(k-1) Q_k; each adjacency orientation has count L^(k-1) P_(k-1) plus O(L^(k-2)), since F_j+F_(j+1)=F_(j+2) and precisely one boundary pair is lost. Two distinct compatible forbidden constraints identify at least two differences between coordinates, leaving at most k-2 free indices. Division by k! therefore gives the stated negative correction; k=2 has a bounded boundary error. Unaligned populations have bounded count errors and forbidden pairs are O(L^(k-1)); the standard shifted subset count gives the conditional limit. The 0 and 1 in the period give positivity as asserted. An independent largest-index digit recursion and exact period convolution reproduce all four pairs of constants and check aligned finite differences for five (k,m) pairs, all residues, via `python3 /workspace/reproductions/frozen_checks.py 4`. This is finite corroboration, not the error-bound proof. The frozen verification file and artifacts/verify.py were inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: The fixed-weight conditional law addresses a different question from density or mere infinitude in all integers. The second coefficient measures the first local exclusion effect and separates repeated indices from Fibonacci adjacency. It supplies reusable exact arithmetic asymptotics across arbitrary fixed weights and moduli and makes explicit when the limiting law is nonuniform, without claiming natural density.
